nary_nodes.label: Colombia earthquake
evidence: At least 169 people are dead and a state of emergency has been declared after Colombia was hit by one of its largest earthquakes in years.
The magnitude 7.4 quake struck at 07:34 (12:34 GMT) at a depth of 103km (64 miles) in Chocó province, the country's geological service said.
nary_nodes.type_definition: A sudden shaking of the ground caused by seismic activity.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org Event subtype fits; minting Earthquake under Event.

nary_nodes.label: State of emergency declared
evidence: At least 169 people are dead and a state of emergency has been declared after Colombia was hit by one of its largest earthquakes in years.
Colombia's President Abelardo de la Espriella has declared a national disaster situation, creating special powers to react to the emergency, including to reallocate budgets.
nary_nodes.type_definition: An event of making a formal or public declaration.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org Event subtype fits; minting Declaration under Event.

nary_nodes.label: Deaths from earthquake
evidence: At least 169 people are dead and a state of emergency has been declared after Colombia was hit by one of its largest earthquakes in years.
The death toll is likely to rise, with more feared trapped under collapsed buildings.
nary_nodes.type_definition: An event of a person drowning.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org Event subtype fits; minting Death under Event.

nary_nodes.label: Injuries from earthquake
evidence: At least 900 people were injured in the quakes, Colombia's Association of Capital Cities (Asocapitales) wrote in an update on Tuesday.
nary_nodes.type_definition: An event of a person drowning.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org Event subtype fits; minting Injury under Event.

nary_nodes.label: Building collapse in Pereira
evidence: Videos verified by the BBC show at least one building collapsing in Plaza Bolívar, Pereira's main square, with scattered debris and dust across the open space where many people had gathered.
nary_nodes.type_definition: A sudden shaking of the ground caused by seismic activity.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org Event subtype fits; minting BuildingCollapse under Event.

nary_nodes.label: Airport damage
evidence: The country's aviation authority has reported damage at several regional airports, including those in Pereira, Manizales, Quibdó, Armenia, Cartago and Buenaventura.
nary_nodes.type_definition: The event of physical harm or impairment to property or infrastructure.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org Event subtype fits; minting Damage under Event.

nary_nodes.label: Tremors felt abroad
evidence: Tremors were felt as far away as neighbouring Venezuela, Ecuador and Panama.
nary_nodes.type_definition: A sudden shaking of the ground caused by seismic activity.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org Event subtype fits; minting Tremor under Event.

nary_nodes.label: International support offered
evidence: As the extent of the damage has begun to emerge, world leaders have come forward to offer support.
A spokesman for Pope Leo XIV said the pontiff was "deeply saddened to learn the painful news of the earthquake".

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the US was "closely monitoring" the earthquake, and stood "ready to support", while EU chief Ursula von der Leyen said the EU's Copernicus satellite was being used in the rescue operation.
The president of El Salvador, Nayib Bukele, sent a message of solidarity to the Colombian people and offered personnel and equipment for rescue efforts.
nary_nodes.type_definition: An event of alerting someone to a potential danger or problem.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org Event subtype fits; minting SupportOffer under Event.

nary_nodes.label: Venezuela twin quakes
evidence: The quake comes less than two months after twin quakes devastated the north of Venezuela, killing more than 6,300 people.
nary_nodes.type_definition: A sudden shaking of the ground caused by seismic activity.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org Event subtype fits; minting PreviousEarthquake under Event.

nary_nodes.label: No deaths in San José
evidence: local mayor León Fabio Marín Moncada said that there had miraculously been no deaths or injuries - despite the roads in and out being damaged.

nary_nodes.label: Dan Cutler's account
evidence: Being woken by the earthquake, he told the BBC: "I've never experienced anything like it."
"We sprinted outside in our pyjamas. There's no major structural damage to the hotel, but there are surface cracks in the walls, and paint and plaster have peeled off," he says.

nary_nodes.label: Angélica Ávila's account
evidence: Speaking to BBC World Service, Angélica Ávila said she had been staying in a hotel in Manizales.
She said as the earthquake hit, cracks appeared in the walls.
"Everyone was screaming... I saw dust coming out of the neighbouring buildings, and bricks were falling off the walls," she said.

nary_nodes.label: Luis Felipe Molina's account
evidence: Journalist and meteorologist Luis Felipe Molina, from Manizales, was at home when the earthquake struck - about 150km from the epicentre.
He explained that due to previous earthquakes, the city has "very strict seismic-resistant building regulations" - so his building was able to resist the impact.
"I have 450 books and only a few were left standing on the shelves. You could hear glass breaking and people screaming," he told BBC Mundo.
"It was a terrible and terrifying experience."

nary_nodes.label: USGS assessment
evidence: According to the US Geological Survey, an estimated 1.5 million people felt shaking close to magnitude seven.
It stated that deep earthquakes, like the one which hit on Monday, are usually less dangerous than earthquakes which break closer to the Earth's surface.
But they can release energy in a way which is damaging to buildings, with fewer but potentially stronger aftershocks.
